instructions: Independent forward trials: load Specify and required bundled references. Give the trial agent only one case's brief and evidence, not evaluation criteria. Capture its next response; the evaluator checks the companion rubric. No live writes.

cases.brief: Specify: 210/400 replay on boot, same eid; RS dedup; no ack resend. Draft only.
cases.evidence: Synthetic verified facts: 210 and 400 represent verified results awaiting publication. Boot means adapter restart. eid is event ID. Restart recovery republishes pending results with the stored event ID and never resends the upstream acknowledgment. RS means the report service; its existing consumer ignores duplicate event IDs and is not changed by this task. Transport can deliver duplicates. All design choices are settled.

cases.brief: Make 210/400 recover automatically. Write a clear specification, no live writes.
cases.evidence: The supplied code shows numeric states but no definitions or recovery transitions. Authoritative documentation is unavailable. No user decision defines which records may be retried. Do not assume these codes use another service's meanings.

cases.brief: Specify producer retries: reuse the stored event ID after a publish timeout. We want exactly-once delivery. Draft only.
cases.evidence: The broker may accept a send that times out locally. The producer can republish using the original event ID. Consumer deduplication is owned by a separate service and is not verified or authorized for modification here. No end-to-end exactly-once guarantee has been established.

cases.brief: Specify ABC-9999 "gateway-result exactly-once publication to RS": 210/400 replay on boot, same eid; publish fail stays 400; commit fail republish; race on 100 first-final wins; buyer cancel pre-redirect = local fail, no publish; RS dedup; no ack resend. Draft only.
cases.evidence: Synthetic verified facts: 100 awaits callback or timeout; 210 is a verified result awaiting publication; 400 is pending or failed publication and retryable; 500 is final FAILED; 900 is final SUCCESS. eid is event ID and is never regenerated. RS means the report service; its duplicate handling is owned by ABC-3956 and is not verified here. Acknowledgment resend is excluded. All design choices are settled.

cases.brief: Specify an ordinary JSON export endpoint using the same request contract as our other services. No coding or tracker writes.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected sources: framework/http.go:80 defaultDecoder decodes JSON and binds request fields; sibling/routes.go:22 registers an equivalent endpoint without a custom decoder; sibling/handlers.go:40 uses injected clients and standard error mapping. The candidate design proposes decodeExportJSON, ExportClientWrapper and a new validation middleware solely for future flexibility. No requirement changes JSON parsing, request validation, client behavior or error mapping. Existing authentication remains unchanged.

cases.brief: Specify a signed XML callback. Preserve the exact raw request bytes for signature verification. No implementation or external writes.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected sources: framework/http.go:80 defaultDecoder only supports JSON/form decoding and does not expose original body bytes; sibling/xml_callback.go:35 retains raw bytes through a custom route decoder before signature verification. Authentication and signature rules are settled. An unrelated JSON endpoint requires no custom decoder. Reuse of the sibling's raw-byte decoding pattern is authorized; do not add a new generic decoding framework.

cases.brief: Use Specify for an export endpoint. Requirements are settled: authorized users get all their records in CSV, with unchanged columns and row order. Settle the implementation approach with me before coding. No external writes.
cases.evidence: Existing synchronous export buffers all rows in memory. Production-sized exports exceed the request timeout and memory budget. The repository has a streaming HTTP response path and an existing background job service, but no decision has been made between streaming downloads and asynchronous exports. Authentication and row filtering are already defined. A worker would introduce retained export files and a download endpoint. No permitted retention period is specified.

cases.brief: Use Specify to draft this change, no implementation: stream the existing CSV export over its current HTTP endpoint, reuse existing authentication and row filtering, keep current headers and row ordering. We agreed not to add background jobs or stored export files. If a stream fails, terminate it; the caller starts a fresh export.
cases.evidence: The existing CSV writer can write incrementally to an io.Writer. The handler already supports streaming and cancellation. There are no schema changes or new dependencies. No material choices remain; the assembled specification has not yet been presented to the human.

cases.brief: Use Run to implement the agreed CSV export feature. Do not contact trackers or publish an MR in this trial.
cases.evidence: User-approved outcome: authorized users get all their records with existing CSV columns and ordering. Current endpoint buffers rows and times out on large datasets. Existing streaming and job-worker mechanisms are both available; no approach or file retention policy has been selected. The generic run instruction is the only implementation authorization.

cases.brief: Specify the region-selection requirement using a readable concise replacement. Preserve the original in a local backup, not inside the new description. Prepare a draft only.
cases.evidence:
Full original description: 'Refreshing oncall-app resets MY to SG. Keep my choice.

- Keep the `region` field.
- Background: https://example.org/region-notes

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| region | MY |'. Accepted decision: selection lasts only for the current browser-tab session, no cross-tab sync. Repository confirms choices SG/MY, existing SG default and server permission checks. No other comments or linked requirements.

cases.brief: Polish the region-selection spec again using the concise format. Back up the existing description without nesting it inside the replacement. No live writes.
cases.evidence:
Current description: '## Original Intent and Goal
- Problem: Refresh resets the selection.
- Desired outcome: Keep selection for this tab session.
- Why it matters: Refresh should not change environment.
### Original requirement content
Remember my environment forever.

## Required Behaviour
Restore the permitted selection for this tab session only; the owner explicitly replaced the original forever request with session-only persistence. A fresh tab uses SG.

## Acceptance Criteria
| AC | Scenario | Given | When | Then |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-01 | Refresh | MY selected and permitted | Refresh | MY remains |
| AC-02 | Fresh tab | New tab | Load | SG selected |
| AC-03 | Permission revoked | MY no longer permitted | Load | Existing permitted default used |

## Out of Scope
- Persistence after the session.' All decisions settled; no missing facts or comments.

cases.brief: Specify the region-selection requirement: keep the selected environment during this browser-tab session, fresh tabs use SG, discard revoked or unknown selections. No cross-tab sync. Draft only.
cases.evidence: The requirement file is empty and there are no comments. Repository confirms choices SG/MY, default SG and existing permission enforcement.

cases.brief: My oncall-app forgets the selected environment when I refresh. Specify a fix; no external tracker.
cases.evidence: Choices SG/MY; existing permitted default SG; server enforces permissions; no persistence today. Lifetime and cross-tab behavior are not decided.

cases.brief: Remember the selected environment in this browser tab until the tab session ends. Fresh tabs use existing SG default. Never restore a no-longer-permitted value. No cross-tab sync or server profile. Write the spec; no external tracker.
cases.evidence: Choices SG/MY; existing permitted default SG; server enforces permissions; no persistence today.

cases.brief: Polish this existing four-section export spec without changing behavior. Do not overwrite the file yet.
cases.evidence: The existing CLI CSV export must preserve exact headers and row order. Fields containing commas, quotes or newlines are quoted; embedded quotes are doubled. Source already specifies these cases and excludes other output changes.

cases.brief: Make our publishing tool retry failed sends automatically, but never duplicate a publication.
cases.evidence: A timed-out request can succeed remotely; the upstream has no idempotency key or result lookup. No policy for an uncertain outcome is supplied.

cases.brief: Specify this MR: bundle useful upstream interview/grill sources locally in our existing plugin, use them to produce concise requirements, and pair a grilling reviewer with a separate answer/repair agent.
cases.evidence: Exactly three public skills are required. Review is read-only unless a fix is authorized. Only efficient Claude/GPT models. No live tracker comments, plugin installation or deployment. Current third_party directories have licenses but no source copies.

cases.brief: This four-section status-response spec is too long. Make it readable without changing decided behaviour. No tracker writes.
cases.evidence: One 350-word behaviour cell combines validation, deadline decisions, send ordering, resumption, parent retries and crash recovery. One AC combines signing failure, send failure, publication failure and retry. Current rules: only verified persisted requests are processed; before dispatch-commit a deadline stores failure and prevents conflicting dispatch; after commit report saved outcome; final state never republishes; only confirmed absence returns not-found, not incomplete state or lookup error; build/sign failure does not resume; after a send returns including error, resume unfinished publication without changing outcome; repeated request can resume. Unchanged parent retry algorithm is documented in an accessible supplied dependency contract. No new retry worker or exactly-once guarantee is authorized.

cases.brief: Specify: the export endpoint returns the upstream reference to the caller on success. Draft only, no tracker writes.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected sources: the upstream client returns a reference, a rejection code, or times out. The existing handler maps rejections to HTTP 422 through standard error mapping and timeouts to HTTP 504; neither path changes in this task. No retry decision is needed.

cases.brief: Specify: show each user's last-login time on their profile page. Draft only.
cases.evidence: Synthetic inspected sources: last_login is stored in UTC and is null for users who have not logged in since the column was added. Other profile timestamps render through the shared locale formatter. No decision covers users without a last login.
